How-to guide

Every screen, step by step, with pictures. It follows the order you'd set up a new company, from your details to your first invoice and pay week.

Before you start

This guide takes a new company from an empty RoadCoda to its first delivered, invoiced and paid load. Go through it in order the first time. After that, jump to whatever you need from the list of contents.

You'll need about an hour for setup, plus the time to fill in the five sheets:

  • Customers: the companies you bill
  • Stop locations: their stores, DCs and yards
  • Trucks & trailers
  • Drivers
  • Office staff

Columns marked * must be filled in. Instructions are on the second tab of each file. Please don't put Social Security or bank account numbers in any sheet.

On the free trial? Everything is switched on except EDI and dock & load-out scanning. You can have up to 25 trucks, and the dispatch assistant has a smaller allowance. The bar across the top of every screen shows the days left. Click What's limited in that bar for the full list.

Finding your way around

The menu down the left side is grouped by the work:

  • Daily: Home, Dispatch, the Route planner, Messages, Loads and Templates. This is where dispatchers live.
  • Money: Invoices, Payroll, Profit, Tolls, IFTA and the QuickBooks export.
  • Safety: incidents, driver files, claims and handbooks.
  • Setup: your company, customers, drivers, equipment, rates and users. It folds away because you won't need it every day.

At the bottom of the menu are What's new (new features, with a count of the ones you haven't seen), Report a problem, the light/dark switch, and Collapse, which shrinks the menu to icons to make room.

Home is today at a glance: loads rolling, stops done, stops running late, delivery issues, and a Needs attention list. Click any load number to open it.

Your Getting started checklist

Open Setup › Getting started. It lists every setup step in order, and each step ticks itself once the data is in, so you always know what's left. Click Open or Go next to a step to jump straight to its screen.

Under the setup steps is a six-week Going live plan: one or two things a week, from running every load through Dispatch to retiring your old spreadsheets.

Tip: Settings check on the same page looks at every setting RoadCoda needs. It tells you what's missing, what won't work because of it, and how to fix it.

Step 1 · Your company

These details print on your invoices, delivery emails and the customer portal. Open Setup › Company:

  1. Company name, as your customers know you. Fill in Name on invoices only if you bill under a different legal name.
  2. Office address and Yard address. Click Check address under each one. Miles and deadhead are measured from the yard.
  3. Time zone, Office phone and Billing email (where customers reply about invoices).
  4. Remit-to address, if checks go somewhere other than the office, and your Payment terms in days.
  5. Logo and Color. Your customers see these on invoices, emails, the tracking page and their portal.
  6. Click Save company details.

Step 2 · Customers and their stores

RoadCoda has two kinds of customer. Bill-to customers are the companies you invoice. Stops (delivery locations) are the stores, DCs and yards your trucks deliver to. Open Setup › Customers:

  1. Click Upload bill-to customers, pick your filled-in Customers sheet, check the preview, then upload.
  2. Click Upload stops and do the same with your Stop locations sheet. One file can cover several customers.
  3. To add one by hand instead, click + New customer.

If a customer has several DCs that each get their own invoice, add each DC as its own customer and set Part of to the main customer. Reports can then show each DC or all of them together.

Tip: A stop with a missing or wrong address shows a warning. Download the stop template for that customer, fix the Address, City, State and Zip columns, and upload it back.

Step 3 · How each customer is billed

From a customer, click Rates & billing settings (or open Setup › Rates and pick the customer). Set up:

  • Customer pricing: a dedicated weekly contract (fixed lines, variable lines and pass-through costs, each value times the volume), or a price per load, stop, mile or hour.
  • Fuel surcharge, if you charge one.
  • Billing window: the day and time each invoice week starts, and whether loads count when they're delivered, started, or by service date.
  • Customer notifications: which delivery emails go out (on the way, running late, delivered, delivery issue).

Once a customer has a rate, loads for that customer are priced automatically. Dispatchers never have to type a price.

Step 4 · Trucks and trailers

Open Setup › Equipment. Click Upload spreadsheet and pick your Trucks & trailers sheet, or click + New unit to add one at a time.

Click a unit to add its toll tag and class, registration and inspection dates, PM interval, and capacity (pallets, weight, cube). The route planner uses the capacity to fill trucks.

On a dedicated account, set the truck's Home account to that customer. The route planner will then use that customer's own trucks first.

The free trial is for up to 25 trucks: tractors, straight trucks, vans and pickups. Trailers don't count.

Step 5 · Drivers

Open Setup › Drivers. Click Upload spreadsheet and pick your Drivers sheet, or click + New driver.

Click a driver to fill in:

  • Pay: per mile, stop, hour, day, load or percent. A driver can have several rates, and a rate can apply to one customer only. Extras like fueling or strapping are set up once under Pay & billing types.
  • CDL and medical card expiry dates. RoadCoda warns you before they run out.
  • Home account, for drivers who work one dedicated customer.

Step 6 · Put the app on each driver’s phone

Drivers don't use passwords. It takes about a minute per driver:

  1. On Drivers, click the driver, then click Set up on a phone. A QR code appears.
  2. The driver points their phone's camera at the QR code and taps the link. The app opens already signed in.
  3. They tap Add to Home screen when the app asks, so it opens like any other app.
  4. Click Print reset card and keep the card in the truck. If the phone ever gets signed out, the driver scans the card and enters their PIN. Every card use shows on Home.

Driver not in the office? Use Copy sign-in link and text it to them, or Email sign-in link.

A driver can switch the app to Spanish with the ES button at the top. It remembers their choice.

Step 7 · Your office team

Open Setup › Users. Click + Invite a user, or Upload spreadsheet with your Office staff sheet. Each person gets an email to set their own password.

For each person, set every screen to Off, View or Edit, or click Use the role's usual screens. Prices, revenue and costs stay hidden unless a person is allowed to see money. Dispatchers normally aren't, and their loads are priced from the rate sheet automatically.

Tip: To make everyone use a code from an authenticator app at sign-in, tick Require two-factor sign-in at the top of this page.

Making loads: three ways

1. One at a time. On Loads or Dispatch, click New load. Pick the customer, add the stops, then click Get miles & price and Save load.

2. From the customer's list. Many customers send a list of stores and windows for the next day. Use Import delivery list on Loads, or open it in the Route planner (next section) and let the planner build the loads.

3. Templates, for runs that repeat. Once a normal load is done, open Templates. Type its load number, give it a name, tick the days it runs, then click Save as template. Each week, Create loads makes the whole week in one click.

On a template's week, click a day to skip it (a holiday) or to add an extra run. Changing a template never changes loads that are already made.

Planning the day: the Route planner

The Route planner decides how many trucks you need, which stops go on each truck, and in what order. It keeps every delivery window and each driver's hours, at the lowest cost to your customer. Open Daily › Route planner:

  1. Pick the Day and the Customer. Trucks start from that customer's DC.
  2. Bring in the stops: Import delivery list (the customer's file), or Create from template and plan for regular runs.
  3. Under Trucks available today, untick any truck that's down.
  4. Click Plan the day.

The plan shows the trucks needed, how full each one is, the miles, the driver hours and the cost. Each truck gets a card with its driver, leave time and every stop in order with its arrival time.

  • If a stop can't be planned, the planner says why in plain words and what would fix it, for example "a truck would need to leave by 3:40". It often gives you a button to try that fix.
  • To try a different leave time for today only, change it here. The customer's normal settings stay as they are.
  • On a dedicated account, the planner uses that account's own trucks and drivers first. It only asks for a rental when they can't carry the day, and says how many.

When you're happy, click Apply this plan. The loads go onto the Dispatch board with their ETAs.

Planning goal: use "Lowest cost to the customer" most days, "Fewest trucks" when you're short of trucks, and "Fewest driver hours" when drivers are short on hours. "Aim for extra time at stops" leaves more room before each window closes.

Running the day: the Dispatch board

Daily › Dispatch is the dispatcher's main screen. The loads that need you are always at the top:

  • Act now: late trucks, detention with no code, and anything you can fix from your desk.
  • Collect after: paperwork still to gather, like a missing POD. It's flagged, but it isn't an emergency.
  • Then every load that's fine. A load drops off the board once it's finished.

The two-letter flags are explained in the legend under the board. For example, TM means times are missing, PD means the POD is missing, and DT means detention isn't coded. Click any load to open the whole trip.

The trip screen

Everything about one load is on one screen: driver, truck and trailer, every stop with its window, arrival and departure times, counts, seal, OS&D and POD.

  • Click any value to change it. Every change is logged along with the value it replaced.
  • + Stop adds a stop mid-trip when a driver calls in.
  • Swap tractor / driver handles a breakdown. Each leg keeps its own truck, driver, miles and pay.
  • Save as template turns this load into a repeating run.

Closing out a trip. When the last stop is done, RoadCoda checks the times, counts, POD, miles and seal. Dispatch clicks Verify as dispatch. Then someone in billing clicks Approve for billing & lock. It has to be a different person, so no one checks their own work. Only locked trips go onto invoices and into payroll.

The driver’s day on the phone

The driver sees one load at a time, with the stops in order. At each stop:

  1. Navigate opens the driver's own map app: Google Maps, Apple Maps, Waze, CoPilot or Sygic. They pick one the first time.
  2. Arrived when they get there. The time is recorded, and your customer can get an email.
  3. Enter the counts, Scan labels with the phone camera or a Bluetooth scanner, and Add photo of the pallets at the door.
  4. Delivered: the receiver signs on the phone. If something's wrong, tap Report issue (short, damaged, over, refused or closed).

The app works with no signal and sends everything when the signal comes back. Drivers can also message dispatch, see their own pay (My pay) and report an accident or injury at the scene, with photos.

Invoices

Open Money › Invoices:

  1. Pick the Customer. The billing window fills in from that customer's settings.
  2. Click Preview to see every locked load in the window, with the contract lines, tolls, detention and extras already on.
  3. Click Create draft invoice, check it, then click Approve.
  4. Click Download PDF to send it, then Mark sent, and Mark paid when the money comes in.

Approved invoices are locked, so what you sent your customer always matches. Customer activity files and the QuickBooks export are under Money too.

Payroll

Open Money › Payroll. The pay week runs Sunday to Saturday and includes only completed, verified trips.

  • Held or paying nothing lists trips that aren't verified yet, or trips with no pay rate. Click Open trip to fix them. A held trip pays in the first open week after it's verified.
  • Click a driver to see every line of their pay.
  • When the week is right, click Approve & lock this week. Then download the file for your payroll company (ADP, Paychex, Paylocity or Gusto) or the QuickBooks entry sheet, and Print pay statements.

Drivers see the same week in the app under My pay.

Your customers’ portal

Give each customer their own login, so they can look things up instead of calling. Open Setup › Customer logins, pick the customer, then choose:

  • Billing: head office. They see all their loads (and their DCs'), stop times and counts, PODs, invoices and the activity file.
  • Delivery: one store or site. They see only the deliveries to their own locations.

Type their name and email, then click Send invite.

Customers never see prices meant for you, other customers, or any office screen. They also get an on-time scorecard tab showing on-time %, time on site, issues and claims.

Reports

  • On-time scorecard (Daily › Scorecard, or the button on a customer): on-time %, how late the late ones were, time on site, issues, claims and miles, by week, month or quarter. Click Print / PDF for your business review.
  • Profit (Money): revenue against driver pay, fuel, tolls and costs, by customer, route, truck and driver.
  • Cost report (Money, for private fleets): what each delivery costs per stop, per case and per mile.
  • Safety dashboard (Safety): incidents per million miles, preventable rate, OSHA logs and estimated cost.

Every report has a download button.

Switching things on and off

RoadCoda has more in it than most companies need on day one. The owner can switch any part on or off under Setup › Features. Switching something off hides it from every screen and keeps its data, so you can switch it back on any time.

Getting help, and keeping RoadCoda

  • Report a problem, at the bottom of the menu, sends us the screen you were on, so we can see what you saw. You get a ticket number to quote.
  • Email support@roadcoda.com any time.
  • What's new shows each new feature and takes you straight to it.
At the end of the free trial: click Keep RoadCoda in the bar at the top and tell us. Everything unlocks right where you left it, with nothing to re-enter. If you don't, RoadCoda becomes view-only for 30 days: you, your drivers and your customers can sign in, look and download, but not add or change anything. After that, your company and its data are removed. We email you 5 days before the trial ends and again before anything is removed.
